                                   4                                   UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

                                   5                                  NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

                                   6

                                   7     TRACY ZIGLER, et al.,                              Case No. 26-cv-00575-EMC
                                   8                    Plaintiffs,
                                                                                            ORDER DENYING PLAINTIFF’S
                                   9             v.                                         ADMINISTRATIVE MOTION TO
                                                                                            SHORTEN DEADLINE
                                  10     LYFT, INC.,
                                  11                    Defendant.                          Docket No. 57
                                  12
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13

                                  14          Plaintiffs have filed suit against Defendant Lyft, Inc., contending in essence that the

                                  15   company engaged in false advertising with respect to its “Priority Pickup” and “Standard”

                                  16   services. See FAC ¶ 3 (alleging that “customers pay more for the promise of a predictable and

                                  17   faster pickup” but the Priority Pickup and Standard rides frequently failed to arrive at the

                                  18   advertised times). Lyft has filed two motions in response to the suit: (1) a motion to dismiss based

                                  19   on lack of standing and (2) a motion to compel arbitration. See Docket Nos. 46-47 (motion to

                                  20   dismiss and motion to compel arbitration). Lyft has expressly noted that the motion to compel

                                  21   arbitration is made “solely in the alternative.” Docket No. 47 (Mot. at 1).

                                  22          Now pending before the Court is an administrative motion filed by Plaintiffs. In the

                                  23   motion, Plaintiffs note that they have propounded discovery on Lyft. Plaintiffs contend the

                                  24   discovery is needed to respond to Lyft’s motion to compel arbitration (i.e., to demonstrate the

                                  25   unconscionability of the arbitration agreement). Plaintiffs argue that:

                                  26   ///

                                  27   ///

                                  28   ///
                                         Case 3:26-cv-00575-EMC             Document 59         Filed 04/20/26      Page 2 of 3




                                   1          (1) Lyft should be ordered to file its discovery responses to the interrogatories and

                                   2               documents requests on shortened time;

                                   3          (2) Because those responses will likely contain objections, Plaintiffs should be permitted

                                   4               to file a motion compel discovery on shortened time;

                                   5          (3) If the Court grants the motion to compel discovery, Lyft should be ordered to provide

                                   6               the discovery no later than the date it files its reply brief in support of its motion to

                                   7               compel arbitration; and

                                   8          (4) Plaintiffs should then, in effect, be given an opportunity to file a sur-reply in opposition

                                   9               to the motion to compel arbitration – i.e., a brief that addresses the discovery produced

                                  10               by Lyft.

                                  11          As an initial matter, the Court notes that Plaintiffs did not sufficiently meet and confer with

                                  12   Lyft before filing this motion. Plaintiffs admit as much in their papers. See Vitale Decl. ¶ 14
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   (noting that “[t]he parties are scheduled to meet and confer Monday morning [April 20, 2026], and

                                  14   will update the Court of any further developments”). The Court also notes that discovery-related

                                  15   issues are to be raised with the Court via joint letter. See

                                  16   https://cand.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/standing-orders/EMC-Standing-Order-Civil-

                                  17   Discovery.pdf (standing order).

                                  18          In addition, Plaintiffs’ proposal is inefficient. If discovery is needed for the motion to

                                  19   compel arbitration, then it makes little sense for there to be briefing on the motion to compel

                                  20   arbitration to be completed and then tack on a sur-reply.

                                  21          Given that Lyft’s motion to compel arbitration is submitted in the alternative to its motion

                                  22   to dismiss for lack of standing, the Court shall proceed as follows.

                                  23          1.       The briefing and hearing schedule for Lyft’s motion to compel arbitration is

                                  24   temporarily VACATED. The Court shall address first Lyft’s motion to dismiss based on lack of

                                  25   standing.

                                  26   ///

                                  27   ///

                                  28   ///
                                                                                           2
                                         Case 3:26-cv-00575-EMC           Document 59        Filed 04/20/26     Page 3 of 3




                                   1          2.      If the Court denies the motion to dismiss, then the parties shall meet and confer

                                   2   regarding the discovery sought with respect to Lyft’s motion to compel arbitration. These

                                   3   discovery disputes should be resolved before the briefing on the motion to compel arbitration is

                                   4   completed and the hearing on the motion to compel arbitration is heard.

                                   5          For the foregoing reasons, the Court denies Plaintiffs’ administrative motion for relief.

                                   6          This order disposes of Docket No. 57.

                                   7

                                   8          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                   9

                                  10   Dated: April 20, 2026

 United States District Court
